accuracy.evidence: Derivatives of all three lab curves (runner d = t², car d = 20t − 2t² to a stop at 50 m, cyclist d = 0.25t³) checked numerically against the stated speeds at every 0.1 s: no mismatch. Worked tangent (1, −3) to (5, 21) gives 24 ÷ 4 = 6 m/s, matching d = t² at 3 s. Matches OpenStax College Physics 2.8: slope of the tangent at a point on a d–t graph is the instantaneous velocity.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips teachers report for this AQA 4.5.6.1.5 skill: dividing distance by time from the origin (average, not instant), reading the graph height as the speed, using a one-second chord instead of a tangent, forgetting to divide rise by run, a ruler that crosses the curve at P, and thinking a flat top means fast.

lab_distinct.evidence: A pivoting ruler laid on a curved distance–time graph: drag P along the curve, drag the ruler handle to turn it, and a red ring marks where a non-tangent cuts through at P or crosses again; plus a stretchable rise ÷ run triangle and a dashed average chord. Unlike flag_deriv's falling-phone secant limit; passes the shingle gate.

lab_teaches.evidence: Step 1 shows 9 ÷ 3 = 3 m/s is wrong by making the learner fit the tangent and read 6 m/s; step 2 sets the 10 m/s tangent beside the 5 m/s average chord; step 3 stretches the triangle from run 1 s to 4 s at a constant 4 m/s; steps 4–5 show the tangent above a braking curve and going flat at 5 s.

predictions.evidence: Each prediction offers the tempting wrong answer first-class: 3 m/s from 9 ÷ 3 and 9 m/s from the height; average equal to instant; a bigger triangle giving a bigger speed; a tangent below a flattening curve; a flat graph meaning the highest speed. The reveal names what was predicted and why the lab disagrees.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Typed speeds are matched to the slip that produces them with the item's own numbers: '4 m/s is 16 m ÷ 4 s: the average speed since the start', 'height of the graph', forward and backward one-second chords, rise without the run, and too steep / too shallow. Items chosen so no two slips coincide (no car t = 1 or cyclist t = 3).

readability.evidence: Kid text grades 1.4 and adult text 7.3 on the pipeline's Flesch–Kincaid check, within the 6.5 and 9.5 limits. Sentences are short, units are given every time (m, s, m/s), and the tangent is defined in plain words before the term is used.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes with no filler phrases; every paragraph carries a rule, a method step or a named mistake. Lab status lines state only numbers and the reason a ruler is not yet a tangent; explanation overlap with other lessons is under the 12% gate.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots of all seven steps checked in dark theme: header, axes labels and P label clear, ruler handle kept inside the plot and beyond the triangle corner. A real CDP touch drag on the ruler line turned it from 1.5 to 6.0 m/s and completed step 1; buttons give a no-drag route.

accessibility.evidence: Canvas aria-label is rewritten on every change with P's time and distance, ruler gradient and why it is or is not a tangent; status is spoken through the live region; every button has an aria-label; challenge input is labelled with its unit and feedback is role=status. axe passes in both themes on desktop and phone.
